battle.name: 布匿戰爭
battle.theater: 西西里島與迦太基沿岸
battle.brief: 公元前264年至前146年，羅馬先後三次與迦太基開戰：墨西拿的仲裁引燃第一次，漢尼拔翻越阿爾卑斯山引發第二次，拒絕羅馬最後通牒招來第三次。卡面的埃及月牙劍是青銅時代的鉤形單刃，在前264年的地中海已廢用逾千年，其弧形砍刃只以伊比利亞 falcata 的形制留在迦太基僱傭兵手上。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 三次布匿戰爭是羅馬共和國與迦太基城邦之間的三度全面衝突，時間由公元前264年橫跨到前146年，戰場從西西里海峽擴展到北非、義大利與伊比利亞。羅馬一方的決策層是元老院與人民大會，戰時最高統帥是兩名帶最高指揮權的年度執政官，各統率一軍；軍隊是公民兵與意大利盟邦兵的混合體，盟邦（拉丁同盟、赫爾尼基人、薩姆尼特人與埃特魯里亞社群）按約提供與公民兵相當的兵力，步兵依波利比烏斯所記的軍團、大隊、手中隊與百人隊編制，每名執政官統率的軍約兩萬步兵（羅馬公民兵一萬、盟邦兵一萬）與六千騎兵，步兵核心是三列縱隊，即少年兵、重裝兵與老兵三段，每段以約二百四十人的手中隊作戰。迦太基一方由百人議會與兩名行政總督掌權，國民軍只是輪替的市民徵召，真正作戰靠僱傭兵與常備兵：伊比利亞與塞爾特伊比利亞步兵、巴利阿里投石手、希臘與敘拉古重裝兵、努米底亞騎兵、北非土著步兵，以及象兵與戰車；海軍是五列槳船隊與環繞北非的港口網，包括帕諾爾莫斯、莉莉巴埃姆、索倫圖姆與阿克拉加斯。第三方角色同樣清楚：第一次戰爭中敘拉古的希耶羅二世與迦太基結盟並在西西里東岸作戰，第二次戰爭中羅馬結盟努米底亞王馬西尼薩，第三次戰爭開戰前烏提卡倒向羅馬並提供港口與船塢，托勒密埃及曾以海軍與金錢支援羅馬，敘拉古則在三次戰爭中先後站在不同一方。
countriesEn: The three Punic Wars were three complete confrontations between the Roman Republic and the city-state of Carthage, running from 264 BC to 146 BC and spreading from the Strait of Messina to North Africa, Italy and Spain. On the Roman side the decision belonged to the Senate and the assembly of the people, and the supreme command in the field was held by two annual consuls carrying imperium, each commanding one army; the troops were a mixture of citizen soldiers and contingents from the Italian allies, who under the arrangements with the Latin League, the Hernici, the Samnites and the Etruscan communities supplied a strength equal to that of the citizen levy, and the infantry was organised in legions, cohorts, maniples and centuries, so that a consular army numbered about 20,000 foot — 10,000 Roman citizens and 10,000 allies — with 6,000 cavalry, the infantry core being the three lines of hastati, principes and pilani, each line fighting in maniples of about 240 men. On the Carthaginian side power rested with a council of a hundred and the two suffetes; the citizen levy was only a rotating conscription, and the real fighting force lay in the mercenaries and the standing troops: Iberian and Celtiberian infantry, Balearic slingers, Greek and Syracusan hoplites, Numidian cavalry, native African infantry, together with elephants and chariots; the navy was a fleet of quinqueremes supported by a ring of North African ports including Panormus, Lilybaeum, Soluntum and Akragas. The part played by third parties is equally clear: in the first war Hiero II of Syracuse was allied to Carthage and fought in eastern Sicily; in the second Rome had the Numidian king Masinissa as an ally; before the third war Utica went over to Rome and supplied a harbour and a shipyard; Ptolemaic Egypt gave the Romans naval and financial support; and Syracuse stood on different sides in each of the three wars.
people: 第一次戰爭的關鍵人物集中在兩件事上。一是公元前264年的墨西拿兵變：駐軍的僱傭兵因分贓不成而反目，殺害城民並佔據城邦，迦太基派來的守將無法驅逐他們，遂向兩方求助；羅馬元老院准許仲裁，執政官阿庇烏斯·克勞狄烏斯·卡烏代克斯在公元前264年作出有利於羅馬的裁決，迦太基守軍被逐，羅馬部隊進駐城內，戰端由此開啟。迦太基方面，卸任行政總督的漢諾在議會發言反對開戰，說即便只是處理一隻老鼠，迦太基也不應為這種事把海軍拉出來，但議會否決了他。二是海戰勝負：執政官蓋烏斯·杜利烏斯於公元前260年指揮米萊海戰，他採用右舷迴旋的接舷陣形，讓羅馬兵藉登艦跳板登上迦太基戰艦；公元前241年，盧塔基烏斯·卡圖盧斯在阿加提斯群島擊潰迦太基殘存艦隊。同一時期在西西里南部與北非維持游擊的哈米爾卡·巴卡是迦太基重建軍力的關鍵，卻在和約之後被排除在和談之外，憤而率軍東渡非洲，並於公元前237至前236年間進入西班牙，埋下第二次戰爭的伏線。第二次戰爭的主角是哈米爾卡之子漢尼拔·巴卡，他以西班牙為基地，於公元前218年率軍翻越阿爾卑斯山，經特雷比亞河與特拉斯梅內湖兩戰，於前216年坎尼會戰全勝；其兄哈斯德魯巴·巴卡在西班牙接應，前207年再率軍翻山，結果在梅陶魯斯河被羅馬的十人委員會包圍殲滅，本人陣亡，使義大利戰局扭轉。迦太基方面的將領有馬果兄弟、馬哈爾巴爾，以及西法克斯與馬西尼薩兩位努米底亞王；羅馬方面，先後有弗拉米尼烏斯、法比烏斯·馬克西穆斯（綽號「拖延期者」，以放棄會戰、鞏固城邑的拖延戰略應對）與馬爾凱魯斯（攻城奪下敘拉古，被稱為「羅馬之劍」），最後由西庇阿·阿非利加努斯接手，在前202年札馬取勝；他的養兄弟西庇阿·盧西烏斯在伊巴利亞戰敗陣亡，是羅馬方面最痛心的損失。第三次戰爭的指揮者是西庇阿·艾米里安；老加圖則是「迦太基必須毀滅」這句話在元老院裡反覆提出的人。史料方面，出身希臘的波利比烏斯以人質身分留在羅馬，親歷第三次戰爭末期並寫成《歷史》，李維與二世紀末的阿庇安則是三次戰爭的主要敘述來源。
peopleEn: The decisive figures of the first war cluster around two matters. The first is the mutiny at Messana in 264 BC: the mercenary garrison, having quarrelled over its plunder, killed the townsmen and seized the city; the Carthaginian commander sent to deal with them could not dislodge them and appealed to both sides; the Roman Senate allowed an arbitration, and the consul Appius Claudius Caudex in 264 BC gave a ruling in Rome's favour, the Carthaginian garrison was expelled and Roman troops entered the city, and from that moment the war was under way. On the Carthaginian side, Hanno, a former boetarch, argued in the council against war, saying that even for the sake of a mouse Carthage ought not to put its fleet to sea, but the council outvoted him. The second is the issue decided at sea: the consul Gaius Duilius fought the battle of Mylae in 260 BC, using a ramming-and-boarding formation in which the Roman ships kept their oars on the disengaged side and the men crossed over on the boarding bridge; in 241 BC Lutatius Catulus destroyed the remaining Carthaginian fleet off the Aegates Islands. Hamilcar Barca, who maintained an insurgency in southern Sicily and later in North Africa, was the key to rebuilding Carthaginian strength, yet he was excluded from the peace negotiations and crossed to Africa in anger, entering Spain in 237–236 BC and thereby planting the seed of the second war. The central figure of the second war was Hamilcar's son Hannibal Barca, who used Spain as his base, crossed the Alps in 218 BC, won at the Trebia and at Lake Trasimene, and won outright at Cannae in 216 BC; his brother Hasdrubal Barca took up the Spanish command and crossed the Alps again in 207 BC, only to be surrounded and destroyed with his own life on the Metaurus, which reversed the situation in Italy. The Carthaginian commanders included the brothers Mago, Maharbal, and the two Numidian kings Syphax and Masinissa; on the Roman side came Flaminius, Fabius Maximus, nicknamed the Delayer, who answered Hannibal by refusing pitched battle, holding the towns and cutting the supply of the Carthaginian raiding parties, and Marcellus, who took Syracuse by siege and was called the Sword of Rome, and finally Scipio Africanus, who won at Zama in 202 BC; his adoptive brother Lucius Scipio fell at Ibera, the gravest Roman loss of the war. The commander of the third war was Scipio Aemilianus, while Cato the Elder was the man who repeated in the Senate that Carthage must be destroyed. As for the sources, Polybius, a Greek who stayed in Rome as a hostage, witnessed the closing years of the third war and wrote the Histories; Livy and Appian, at the end of the second century AD, are the principal narrators of the three wars.
kits: 卡面這件埃及月牙劍屬青銅時代的兵器，比希臘人的直劍早了一千多年：考古上最早的實例可追溯到那爾達二期，約公元前三千一百年至前二千九百年，出土的是銅合金的單刃弧形刀身，柄部加寬以便雙手握持，刃口向內彎曲，砍入之後順著弧度拖出即可，不必像直劍那樣拔出再砍；中王國與新王國時期它仍在埃及軍隊中，到第二中間期則主要出現在喜克索斯人以及來自利比亞、舍爾登的僱傭兵手中，並沿地中海東岸傳播。公元前264年的地中海世界早已不用這種形制：埃及的軍隊改持直身短劍與長矛，希臘與色雷斯在前六世紀另行發展出弧形單刃的 kopis，迦太基僱傭兵常用的伊比利亞 falcata（波利比烏斯有記載）是另一支延續，但都不再是月牙劍本身。與此同時真正決定布匿戰爭勝負的裝備分屬兩套體系。羅馬步兵的骨架是重標槍 pilum——槍桿為碳化木、長約二米、連鐵矛頭約一公斤，擲出後仍可作為近身格擋的長矛；配備約六十厘米長的鐵質短劍 gladius、寬約六十厘米、高約一百二十厘米的弧形大盾 scutum，以及鎖子甲與魚鱗甲，另有短程投槍 veles 與擲石用的投石索。迦太基步兵以伊比利亞 falcata、小圓盾 caetra 與大型橢圓盾為主，配長矛與投槍，巴利阿里人用投石索打鉛彈，努米底亞騎兵持長槍與小圓盾作高速衝擊。攻城方面雙方都備有可移動的攻城塔、蒙皮包覆的撞槌、雲梯、活動木廊、龜甲陣與土壘 agger，羅馬更以環形營牆圍困城市。海戰是這場戰爭最特別的一章：羅馬在公元前264年從一艘俘獲的敘拉古船上取得登艦跳板 corvus 的樣式，造出可折疊的接舷橋；主力是五列槳船與五十槳船，裝有青銅撞角 rostrum 與甲板上的配重式投石機與石弩；狄奧尼修斯一世與其子在前265年與前262年兩度在西西里海峽架設浮橋，試圖切斷迦太基與敘拉古的聯繫。運輸與補給方面，羅馬依賴牛拉的車隊、騾隊與海運，糧食大量取自西西里與北非。
kitsEn: The Egyptian khopesh on the card belongs to the Bronze Age and is more than a millennium older than the Greek straight sword: the earliest archaeological examples go back to the Naqada II period, roughly 3100 to 2900 BC, and what is recovered is a single-edged copper-alloy blade curved outward, with a grip widened for two hands and an inner edge so shaped that once the blow has landed the weapon can be dragged out along its own curve instead of being pulled back and swung again; it was still carried by Egyptian armies under the Middle and New Kingdoms, and in the Second Intermediate Period it appears above all in the hands of the Hyksos and of Libyan and Sherden mercenaries, spreading along the eastern Mediterranean shore. The Mediterranean of 264 BC had long since abandoned the form: Egyptian troops had taken to straight short swords and spears, the Greeks and Thracians had developed the single-edged curved kopis from the sixth century BC, and the Iberian falcata used by Carthaginian mercenaries, which Polybius describes, is a separate continuation of the same idea, but none of them is the khopesh itself. The equipment that actually decided the Punic Wars belonged to two rival systems. The backbone of the Roman infantry was the heavy javelin, the pilum, with a shaft of carbonised wood about two metres long and about a kilogram with its iron head, which could be thrown and then used as a thrusting weapon at close quarters; this went with the iron short sword, the gladius, about sixty centimetres long, the large curved shield, the scutum, roughly sixty centimetres wide and a hundred and twenty high, mail and scale armour, and the short throwing spear, the veles, together with the stone sling. Carthaginian infantry fought with the Iberian falcata, the small round caetra and the large oval shield, with spears and javelins; Balearic slingers used the sling with lead bullets, and Numidian cavalry carried a long spear and a small round shield for the charge. For siege work both sides had movable towers, hide-covered rams, ladders, the moving gallery, the testudo and the earthen agger, and Rome added the circumvallation to ring a besieged city. The naval dimension is the most distinctive chapter of the war: in 264 BC the Romans took the model of the boarding bridge, the corvus, from a captured Syracusan ship and produced a folding version of it; the backbone of the fleets was the quinquereme and the penteconter, fitted with a bronze rostrum and with catapults and stone-throwing ballistae on deck; and Dionysius I and his son twice bridged the Sicilian strait, in 265 and again in 262 BC, in an attempt to cut Carthage off from Syracuse. On the transport and supply side Rome relied on ox-drawn carts, mule trains and the sea, and drew a large part of its grain from Sicily and North Africa.
tactics: 三次戰爭的戰術面貌彼此不同。第一次的核心是海上接舷戰與海岸攻城的結合。羅馬在沒有海軍的國度裡現造主力艦隊：公元前264年在一百天內建成一百艘五列槳船與五十艘五十槳船，徵集一萬名槳手，並在俘獲的敘拉古戰船上取樣，改出可折疊的登艦跳板。公元前260年的米萊海戰，執政官杜利烏斯把右舷朝向敵陣，令羅馬兵在接舷瞬間搭橋登船，海上戰爭的勝負因而第一次由登船肉搏決定。公元前256年的埃克諾穆斯海戰，羅馬以兩翼分進的雙縱隊包抄迦太基的橫列，一舉取得制海權；此後戰役重心移到北非沿岸，羅馬在帕諾爾莫斯建立基地，圍攻阿克拉加斯。公元前262至前261年的阿克拉加斯攻防戰留下兩個典型畫面：迦太基主帥哈尼拔·吉斯柯夜襲羅馬營地得手，而羅馬軍在夜間因營中到處是酒而失去秩序；隨後羅馬靠一條貼著城牆的攻擊道迂迴進兵，奪回城區——這是羅馬早期最接近攻城技術的一次得手。第二次戰爭則是機動作戰與包殼戰術的示範。漢尼拔從西班牙出發時就已決定不在義大利正面取決，他以梯隊拉長行軍縱隊翻越阿爾卑斯山，隊形被迫成單列，騎兵與戰象最後通過；特雷比亞河一役，他利用河谷地形與埋設的伏兵消耗羅馬的推進縱隊；公元前217年特拉斯梅內湖一役，漢尼拔在湖岸狹窄地帶設伏，全殲弗拉米尼烏斯的軍隊；公元前216年坎尼會戰，他讓中央縱隊連續進攻以消耗羅馬主力，待羅馬兩翼越過本陣推進後，迦太基騎兵回轉包抄，非洲步兵再在羅馬縱隊背後合攏，完成雙重包圍。羅馬的應對是三段式：先是法比烏斯·馬克西穆斯的拖延戰略，放棄會戰、鞏固城邑、切斷迦太基游擊戰的補給；再是馬爾凱魯斯與西庇阿的軍制改革，把作戰單位由縱隊改為大隊與百人隊，讓三列縱隊可分段應戰並輪替掩護，輔以新式小型標槍與更密的陣形；公元前207年更由十人委員會集中兵力，在梅陶魯斯河切斷哈斯德魯巴的縱隊。第三次戰爭回到圍城術：羅馬在城外築環形營牆與塹壕、修築土壘、建起與城牆等高的射擊台，並在港池築堤封鎖；迦太基則以出海反擊、掘地道反制、襲擾羅馬糧道與向外求援來拖住對方。
tacticsEn: The tactical character of the three wars differs sharply. The first centred on the combination of boarding fights at sea and siege operations ashore. Rome, a country without a fleet, had to build one: in 264 BC it completed a hundred quinqueremes and fifty penteconters in a hundred days, levied ten thousand rowers, and took the model of the folding boarding bridge from a captured Syracusan ship. At Mylae in 260 BC the consul Duilius turned his right side to the enemy and had the Roman soldiers cross over on the bridge at the moment of contact, so that the issue at sea was decided for the first time by the melee on the enemy's deck. At Cape Ecnomus in 256 BC the Romans deployed in two wings, wrapping the Carthaginian line, and gained command of the sea; the weight of the war then moved to the North African coast, where Rome established a base at Panormus and besieged Akragas. The fighting over Akragas in 262–261 BC left two textbook images: the Carthaginian commander Hannibal Gisco won the night attack on the Roman camp, and the Roman soldiers lost their order in the dark because wine was everywhere in the camp; the Romans then recovered the city by turning the assault along a covered way that ran close under the wall, which is among the closest thing to a technical siege success in Rome's early history. The second war was a demonstration of movement and of the encirclement tactic. Hannibal had decided on the march out of Spain not to force a decision in Italy proper: he lengthened the column and crossed the Alps, the formation forced into single file, the cavalry and the elephants crossing last; at the Trebia he used the ground of the valley and an ambush to grind down the Roman column; at Lake Trasimene in 217 BC he ambushed the Roman army in the narrow strip by the shore and destroyed it; and at Cannae in 216 BC he fed his centre in to wear down the Roman line, and when the Roman wings had pushed past his own formations the Carthaginian cavalry wheeled back to envelop, and the African infantry closed the line behind the Roman centre, completing a double encirclement. Rome's answer came in three stages: first the delaying strategy of Fabius Maximus, refusing pitched battle, holding the towns and cutting the supply of the Carthaginian raiders; then the military reform of Marcellus and Scipio, changing the tactical unit from the maniple to the cohort and century, allowing the three lines to engage in sections and relieve one another, supported by new light javelins and a denser order; and in 207 BC the concentration of a commission of ten, which cut Hasdrubal's column on the Metaurus. The third war returned to siegecraft: the Romans ringed the city with a circumvallation and a ditch, raised earthen works, built firing platforms as high as the walls, and closed the harbour with a mole; the Carthaginians answered with sorties by sea, counter-mines, raids on the Roman supply lines and appeals for outside help, seeking only to delay.
data: 可引用的數字大致如下。三次戰爭的時長：第一次公元前264至前241年，約二十三年；第二次前218至前201年，約十七年；第三次前149至前146年，圍城三年。造艦的數字來自波利比烏斯：公元前264年羅馬計畫建造一百艘五列槳船與五十艘五十槳船，徵集一萬名槳手，五列槳船每艘配三百名槳手、五十槳船一百二十名，船體在百日內完工。編制方面，每名執政官統率的軍約兩萬步兵與六千騎兵；一個百人隊約一百二十人，一個手中隊約二百四十人；軍隊每日行軍約三十羅馬里，折合四十四公里上下，分五個小時的軍行完成。埃克諾穆斯海戰是古代地中海規模最大的海戰之一，波利比烏斯記載雙方投入的五列槳船合計逾五百艘，迦太基方面折損七百艘、人員約二萬；七百艘顯然高於實際，多數研究認為應在數百艘之譜，羅馬方面的損失則被描述為相對輕微。阿加提斯群島海戰通常定於公元前241年3月10日，羅馬以主力艦隊封住迦太基港池，迦太基派出的殘存艦隊在交戰中全滅。第二次戰爭方面，漢尼拔翻越阿爾卑斯山時的軍隊約二萬六千步兵、六千騎兵與二十六頭戰象，經特雷比亞河與坎尼會戰後銳減至兩萬上下；坎尼會戰羅馬方面投入約八萬步兵與六千騎兵，波利比烏斯記載羅馬陣亡與被俘約五萬至七萬人，迦太基方面損失約五千七百人；特拉斯梅內湖一役羅馬方面被投入的兵力約三萬至四萬。第三次戰爭的守方數字來自阿庇安：羅馬在非洲的兵力約八萬四千，迦太基城牆主體厚約九米、高十五至二十米，牆周長三十五公里以上，牆內營房可容二萬四千兵。戰俘贖金有明確記錄：公元前241年和約規定自由人每人五德拉克瑪、奴隸十德拉克瑪。第二次戰爭的和約賠款為一萬塔蘭特銀，分五十年支付。兵器本身可引用的考古數字：紐約大都會藝術博物館所藏的青銅月牙劍定年約公元前三千一百年至前二千九百年，刃長約五十厘米。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly as follows. The length of the three wars: the first from 264 to 241 BC, about twenty-three years; the second from 218 to 201 BC, about seventeen years; the third from 149 to 146 BC, three years of siege. The shipbuilding figures come from Polybius: in 264 BC the Romans planned a hundred quinqueremes and fifty penteconters, levied ten thousand rowers, fitted each quinquereme with three hundred rowers and each penteconter with a hundred and twenty, and completed the hulls in a hundred days. As to organisation, each consular army was about 20,000 foot and 6,000 cavalry; a century was about 120 men and a maniple about 240; the army covered about thirty Roman miles a day, some forty-four kilometres, in five marching hours. The battle of Cape Ecnomus was among the largest sea battles of the ancient Mediterranean, and Polybius records more than five hundred quinqueremes committed on both sides, with the Carthaginians losing seven hundred ships and about 20,000 men; seven hundred ships is plainly above the possible, and most studies put the real loss in the hundreds, while the Roman losses are described as comparatively slight. The battle of the Aegates Islands is usually dated to 10 March 241 BC, when the Roman main fleet sealed the Carthaginian harbours and the surviving Carthaginian squadron was destroyed in the engagement. For the second war: Hannibal's army at the crossing of the Alps was about 26,000 foot, 6,000 horse and twenty-six elephants, and had been reduced to some twenty thousand after the Trebia and Cannae; at Cannae the Romans committed about 80,000 foot and 6,000 cavalry, and Polybius records fifty to seventy thousand Romans killed or captured against Carthaginian losses of about 5,700; the force committed at Trasimene was between thirty and forty thousand men. The defensive figures for the third war come from Appian: the Roman force in Africa about 84,000 strong, the main Carthaginian wall about nine metres thick and fifteen to twenty metres high, the circuit of the walls exceeding thirty-five kilometres, and barracks inside the walls able to hold 24,000 men. The ransom of prisoners is exactly recorded: the peace of 241 BC set it at five drachmas for a free man and ten for a slave. The indemnity of the second war was ten thousand silver talents, payable over fifty years. For the weapon on the card the archaeological figures are: the bronze khopesh in the Metropolitan Museum of Art is dated to about 3100–2900 BC, with a blade of some fifty centimetres.
cause: 三次開戰的近因各有一套，深層的動力卻是同一件事：西地中海的航線與穀物。公元前264年的直接起因在墨西拿。駐軍的馬默提尼僱傭兵因分贓不成而反目，殺害城民、佔據城邦，迦太基無力驅逐，遂向羅馬求援；羅馬元老院准許仲裁，執政官阿庇烏斯·卡烏代克斯的裁決把墨西拿判給羅馬的盟友，迦太基守軍被逐，羅馬部隊進駐。迦太基議會在漢諾的「一隻老鼠」發言之後仍決定開戰，羅馬隨即面對一個沒有艦隊的國度被迫造船，海戰成為整場戰爭的主軸；敘拉古的希耶羅二世與迦太基結盟，更把西西里東岸的強權拖進戰局。前241年第一次戰爭以迦太基求和告終，和約卻沒有解決結構性矛盾：迦太基失去海外用兵權，賠款一萬塔蘭特銀分五十年支付，羅馬則接管西西里島並把戰線推向西班牙。第二次戰爭的前因因此落在西班牙：公元前225年羅馬以使團干涉迦太基在伊比利亞的擴張，前221年薩貢托陷落，前218年漢尼拔越過埃布羅河，羅馬隨即宣戰。公元前150年第三次開戰的近因是羅馬的最後通牒：使團要求迦太基交出涉入塞琉古盟約的哈斯德魯巴、繳出部分城防武裝，繼而要求居民撤到城外十英里並拆毀城市；迦太基殺死使團、宣戰，羅馬於前149年正式宣戰並在烏提卡登陸。往深一層看，羅馬與迦太基的矛盾集中在三件事上：西西里島的穀物與稅收、迦太基商業財富對羅馬中小土地所有者的衝擊，以及雙方都想控制海峽航線與西部的銀礦；而元老院與平民黨都需要一場對外勝利來消化國內的失分，這也是三次戰爭都能被接受的原因。
causeEn: Each of the three wars had its own immediate occasion, but the deep motive behind all three was the same: the shipping lanes and the grain of the western Mediterranean. The immediate occasion of 264 BC lay at Messana. The Mamertine mercenaries there, having quarrelled over their plunder, killed the townsmen and seized the city; Carthage could not dislodge them and turned to Rome; the Roman Senate granted an arbitration, and the ruling of the consul Appius Claudius Caudex awarded Messana to Rome's allies, the Carthaginian garrison was driven out and Roman troops moved in. The Carthaginian council, after Hanno's speech about a mouse, nevertheless decided on war, and Rome was thereby forced to build a fleet it did not have, which made the sea battle the axis of the whole contest; Hiero II of Syracuse allied with Carthage and drew the great power of eastern Sicily into the war. The first war ended in 241 BC with Carthage asking for terms, but the treaty settled nothing structural: Carthage lost the right to make war overseas and owed ten thousand silver talents over fifty years, while Rome took Sicily and pushed the line of war towards Spain. The cause of the second war therefore lay in Spain: in 225 BC Rome interfered by embassy in Carthaginian expansion in Iberia, Saguntum fell in 221 BC, and when Hannibal crossed the Ebro in 218 BC Rome declared war. The occasion of the third war in 150 BC was the Roman ultimatum: the envoys demanded the handing over of Hasdrubal, who was entangled with the Seleucid alliance, and the surrender of part of the city's armour, and then required the population to move ten miles out of the walls and the city itself to be pulled down; the Carthaginians murdered the envoys and declared war, and Rome formally declared war in 149 BC, landing at Utica. Deeper down, the quarrel between Rome and Carthage turned on three things: the grain and the taxes of Sicily, the impact of Carthaginian commercial wealth on the small landholders of Rome, and the wish of both parties to control the straits and the silver of the west; and the Senate and the popular party both needed a foreign victory to absorb their domestic losses, which is why all three wars could be accepted at home.
impact: 布匿戰爭的結果不只是一個迦太基的消失，它改寫了地中海世界的權力結構，也改寫了羅馬自己。第一次戰爭之後，羅馬得到西西里島並把它變成第一個行省，國家的海軍從此不再是臨時召集的水上民兵，而成為常設兵種；迦太基雖敗而未亡，靠農業與商業在戰後二十年間恢復，甚至比戰前更富，這說明一個城邦的國力並不取決於一場戰爭的勝負。第二次戰爭把羅馬的邊界推到西班牙，銀礦與物資從此源源流入義大利，也把義大利的農民徵召制度推到極限：公民兵長期遠征，土地兼併加速，這正是後來羅馬兵制改徵募制的背景。漢尼拔則成為兵家的標準範本，其越嶺迂迴、以中央消耗加兩翼包抄的戰法，在此後兩千年的軍事著作中反覆被引用；公元前202年的札馬勝利也確立了羅馬的戰役指揮模式。第三次戰爭之後，西地中海再沒有可以與羅馬抗衡的國家：迦太基土地被宣布為公地，城市被有意拆毀、禁止重建，約五萬人被販為奴隸；北非的龐特語與地方習俗並未被禁止，羅馬以公地形式接管，卻留下「迦太基必須毀滅」這句話作為政治資源，日後反覆被用來攻擊對手。到羅馬共和末期，兩百年間的雙強對抗已經教會羅馬如何取得霸權，也留下最嚴重的隱患：迦太基滅亡之後，義大利的中小土地所有者失去戰爭紅利，僱傭軍成了唯一的兵源，帝國的財政與土地問題於是在共和國解體時爆發。
impactEn: The outcome of the Punic Wars was not merely the disappearance of Carthage: it rewrote the balance of power in the Mediterranean world, and it rewrote Rome itself. After the first war Rome held Sicily and turned it into its first province, and the fleet of the state ceased to be an ad hoc levy of seamen and became a standing arm of the service; Carthage, though beaten, was not destroyed, and recovered through agriculture and commerce so thoroughly that within twenty years it was richer than before, which shows that the strength of a city-state does not turn on the result of a single war. The second war carried the Roman frontier into Spain, and silver and goods from there flowed into Italy without end; it also pushed the Italian system of citizen recruitment to its limit, for the citizens were away for years and the consolidation of land went on apace, the very background to the later change of the Roman army to recruitment by enlistment. Hannibal became the standard model for the writers on war, and his marching by the long way round, his grinding of the centre and his envelopment of the flanks were cited again and again in the military literature of the two thousand years that followed; the Roman victory at Zama in 202 BC likewise settled the Roman model of command in the field. After the third war there was no state left in the western Mediterranean able to match Rome: the land of Carthage was declared public land, the city was deliberately levelled and rebuilding forbidden, and some fifty thousand people were sold into slavery; the Punic language and the local customs of North Africa were not banned, and Rome took the place over in the form of public land, but the sentence that Carthage must be destroyed remained a political resource to be used again and again against a rival. By the end of the Roman Republic, two centuries of contest between the two powers had taught Rome how to win a hegemony, and had left the gravest of hidden dangers: once Carthage was gone the small landholders of Italy lost the profits of war, the mercenary was the only soldier available, and the fiscal and agrarian problems of the empire broke out as the republic came apart.
result: 公元前241年，羅馬在阿加提斯群島海戰中取勝，迦太基求和：歸還羅馬俘虜、按自由人每人五德拉克瑪與奴隸十德拉克瑪的標準贖回被俘者、放棄西西里以外的外島與據點、拆毀部分城防，羅馬則在島上扶植拉丁城市並取得西西里的統治；然而哈米爾卡·巴卡拒絕和約，繼續在西西里南部抵抗，之後率軍渡海到北非，再於公元前237至前236年進入西班牙，把西班牙的基地變成迦太基重建國力的來源。公元前202年札馬會戰後，漢尼拔回到迦太基，議和條件是：西班牙與西西里之外的海外領土歸羅馬，賠款一萬塔蘭特銀分五十年支付，迦太基不得在海外用兵，軍隊縮減、海軍解散；羅馬人把這份和約刻在銅板上，成為「平等條約」的樣本。戰爭結束後接踵而至的是傭兵戰爭（公元前205至前203年）：羅馬在戰後財政枯竭之際無法付清傭兵的欠餉，軍隊在圖里戰役之後起兵，轉而包圍自己的都城，最後由執政官馬尼利烏斯在迦太基戰線上以軍糧法化解。利比亞戰爭（公元前149至前146年）隨之而來：迦太基在哈斯德魯巴·吉斯柯的改革下以全民徵召重整軍力，羅馬視之為違約，前150年提出最後通牒，前146年破城，迦太基被焚毀、居民被販為奴隸、廢墟被宣布為公地並禁止重建；哈斯德魯巴在得到保命許諾後仍自殺，其家屬退入神廟自焚，西庇阿·艾米里安因此獲得「阿非利加努斯」的稱號。三次布匿戰爭至此全部結束，羅馬成為西地中海唯一的主人。
resultEn: In 241 BC the Romans won the battle of the Aegates Islands and Carthage asked for terms: the Roman prisoners were given back, the captives were ransomed at five drachmas for a free man and ten for a slave, the islands and outposts outside Sicily were abandoned, and part of the defences of the city were pulled down, while Rome planted Latin cities on the island and assumed the rule of Sicily; Hamilcar Barca, however, refused the settlement, kept up the resistance in southern Sicily, then crossed the sea to Africa and in 237–236 BC entered Spain, turning a Spanish base into the source of Carthaginian recovery. After the battle of Zama in 202 BC Hannibal returned to Carthage and the terms were settled: Spain and the overseas possessions outside Sicily went to Rome, an indemnity of ten thousand silver talents was to be paid over fifty years, Carthage was not to make war overseas, its army was reduced and its fleet disbanded; the Romans engraved the settlement on bronze, and it became a model of the equal treaty. The Mercenary War followed at once (205–203 BC): in the financial exhaustion of the peace the Romans could not pay the arrears due to their soldiers, the army rose after the battle of Turii and besieged its own capital, and the affair was only settled by the consul Manilius and the law on military service while the Roman army stood on the Carthaginian front. The Libyan War came next (149–146 BC): under the reform of Hasdrubal Gisco Carthage rearmed itself by a levy of the whole citizen body, Rome treated this as a breach, put forward the ultimatum in 150 BC, and in 146 BC took the city; Carthage was burnt, the inhabitants were sold into slavery, the site was declared public land and rebuilding was forbidden; Hasdrubal, having been given a promise of his life, still killed himself, and his family burned themselves in the temple, and Scipio Aemilianus thereby won the name of Africanus. With that the three Punic Wars were over, and Rome stood as the sole master of the western Mediterranean.
